timeline.public-api.surface.rationale: Timeline public exports remain consumable by the route surface.

timeline.strip.math.rationale: Range URL transitions preserve server-owned millisecond bounds.

timeline.shared.presentation.rationale: Shared event markers retain their semantic presentation.

timeline.filters.url.rationale: Toolbar filters serialize canonically and restore with browser history.

timeline.lanes.presentation.rationale: Lane grouping and order are rendered from the authorized projection.

timeline.live.stream.rationale: Live frame merging preserves bounded snapshot identity and ordering.

timeline.list.detail.rationale: List events open the detail sheet without losing selected-event URL state.

timeline.strip.controls.rationale: Range picker, lens controls, keyboard navigation, and reduced motion are exercised at the route surface.

timeline.swimlanes.grouping.rationale: Swimlane grouping, sorting, and pin affordances remain capability-gated.

timeline.toolbar.controls.rationale: Toolbar controls expose only server-described choices and preserve focus behavior.

timeline.toolbar.state.rationale: Activity and problem projections map to stable URL filter state.

timeline.adapter.source.rationale: The adapter maps authenticated snapshot, overview, and stream contracts without source-runtime imports.

timeline.local-scrubber.rationale: Local source selection remains route-capability gated.

timeline.retained-overview.rationale: Retained overview buckets and coverage are created from an authorized server aggregation.

timeline.view.integration.rationale: Timeline view controls compose through the product surface rather than the upstream runtime.

timeline.url.history.rationale: Back, forward, replace-history, and deep-link state use one URL state model.

timeline.source-context.rationale: Source selection and transport composition remain isolated in the product adapter.

timeline.source-contract.rationale: HTTP capability, snapshot, overview, and stream request shapes are validated at the product boundary.

applications.catalog.batch-runtime.rationale: Catalog cards and table rows must render batch runtime, retained run outcome, and deterministic attention ordering from a typed product projection.

applications.catalog.delivery-status.rationale: The adapter must keep runtime readiness and deployment-source delivery state distinct instead of deriving either in the browser.

applications.detail.scope-tabs.rationale: Application, workload, and detail-tab URL state must round-trip through one route controller without mounting the wrong scope.

applications.detail.overview-projection.rationale: The Python response schema must make source, workload, batch, relationship, and completeness evidence explicit before the overview can render it.

applications.detail.topology.rationale: Authorized application topology, workload focus, resource navigation, and source-inventory differences require route-level interaction coverage.

applications.detail.history.rationale: Authorized application history must preserve partial-source evidence, deployment anchors, incidents, and source links without exposing provider payloads.

applications.detail.identity-switcher.rationale: Environment-instance switching, popover dismissal, focus, and reduced-motion behavior must be exercised in the product route.

applications.detail.parity.rationale: The existing generic five-tab detail test is expanded into application-detail parity coverage only after its typed projection exists.

applications.public-api.rationale: The route-level application tab and workload-scope contract remains consumable without importing the isolated upstream component barrel.

gitops.detail.operation-gate.rationale: The provider-neutral detail surface renders server-observed operation gating and refresh/sync capability reasons without creating a browser command.

gitops.detail.revision-meta.rationale: The detail surface renders only the server-projected source revision; author and signature evidence remain a later provider integration.

gitops.graph-filter.input.rationale: Topology resource filtering must use the shared accessible input boundary and preserve the controlled query across graph updates.

gitops.list.operation-gate.rationale: Fleet row actions must make the operation-in-progress reason visible and must not submit a second conflicting Argo sync.

gitops.list.search-input.rationale: GitOps list search must remain a controlled, keyboard-accessible query without duplicating raw input behavior.

gitops.list.labels-input.rationale: Label search and AND-selection must preserve focus, outside dismissal, and the server-authorized row set.

gitops.managed-resources.disclosure.rationale: Managed-resource and kind disclosures must retain lazy content, resource navigation, and reduced-motion-safe state changes.

gitops.sync-countdown.duration.rationale: A controller-provided duration and observed timestamp must produce a safe countdown without browser-derived controller state.

gitops.sync-options.payload.rationale: Application and resource sync payloads must preserve selective-sync safety invariants and typed command identity at the adapter boundary.

gitops.sync-options.validation.rationale: Selective dry-run state, validation reset, operation gating, and outcome disclosure must be exercised through the product route.

gitops.sync-options.feedback.rationale: Dry-run success, failure, inconclusive, and redacted diagnostic feedback must be rendered from a typed server result.

gitops.insights.resource-diff.rationale: A revision-bound desired-versus-live diff must handle loading, redaction, errors, fullscreen dismissal, and no-change evidence.

gitops.insights.resource-filters.rationale: Resources search, OR facets, all-versus-declared inventory, apply order, and status sorting require route-level projection coverage.

gitops.insights.focus-disclosure.rationale: Issue-to-resource focus must clear incompatible local filters, scroll once, expand diagnostics, and respect reduced-motion preference.

gitops.insights.resource-actions.rationale: Resource open, missing-source navigation, selective sync eligibility, and inline drift/event disclosure must be capability-gated by the projection.

gitops.insights.availability.rationale: Application detail renders revision-bound comparison availability and an explicit unavailable reason without inventing a resource diff.

gitops.insights.helpers.rationale: Typed resource search, facet predicates, eligibility, and severity ordering must be deterministic outside rendering.

gitops.insights.status-summary.rationale: A synchronized but degraded resource must remain visible as degraded in the GitOps summary projection.

gitops.insights.disclosure-motion.rationale: Historical issue, raw-error, compact issue, and resource disclosures must retain semantic expanded state with reduced-motion-safe transitions.

gitops.tree.icon-and-portal.rationale: Topology node icons must use the shared resource registry and never make the root resource a recursive detail portal.

gitops.provider-assets.provenance.rationale: The product-owned provider asset registry and copied bytes remain pinned to immutable upstream source hashes without importing the isolated source runtime.

build.entrypoint.baseline.rationale: The standalone product package and document root retain an explicit compatibility baseline without importing or publishing the isolated upstream runtime.

helm.release-list.scope.rationale: The scoped release list must show only inventory-observed Helm storage metadata and must disclose incomplete label coverage.

helm.release-detail.availability.rationale: Release detail must keep history metadata separate from unavailable manifest, values, owned-resource, and command integrations.

helm.release-contract.rationale: The Python HTTP boundary must apply workspace and inventory-read scope before emitting any storage metadata.

traffic.overview.unavailable.rationale: The route must show authorized scope freshness and explicit collector absence; it must never turn unavailable traffic evidence into zero counts or an empty graph.

traffic.overview.contract.rationale: The Python boundary must apply workspace and inventory-read scope to the normalized overview and keep unavailable flow fields null.

traffic.filters.collector-gate.rationale: Namespace, protocol, and status flow filters remain unavailable until collector-backed flow records and filter facets are specified by the server.

cost.overview.unavailable.rationale: The Cost surface must disclose authorized scope and collector absence without rendering a currency, zero amount, projection, or recommendation.

cost.overview.contract.rationale: The Python boundary applies workspace and inventory-read scope and keeps every monetary field null until a provider-backed observation exists.

topology.graph.contract.rationale: The Python topology boundary must keep the authorized cluster scope, graph evidence, unavailable projection, and server refresh policy explicit.

topology.graph.surface.rationale: The resource relationship surface must render only the authorized evidence graph and disclose partial or unavailable results.

topology.graph.freshness.rationale: The relationship frame must use the server-provided refresh interval and retain the last verified graph during a refresh.

topology.controls.scope.rationale: Topology view, grouping, and visibility controls require route-level scope, focus, keyboard, and reduced-motion coverage before they can be claimed.

topology.search.scope.rationale: Topology search must prove selected-resource navigation and keyboard dismissal against the current authorized graph scope.

topology.kind-icon.registry.rationale: Every observed resource kind must resolve through one product-owned icon registry, including workflow and monitoring CRDs, with a deterministic unknown-kind fallback.

topology.workflow-card.contract.rationale: Workflow entrypoint, template count, endpoint count, and grouped-card subtitle evidence require typed Python fields before a browser presentation can consume them.

topology.public-composition.rationale: Topology chrome remains reachable through the product route composition without importing the isolated source package barrel or runtime.

topology.breadcrumb.keyboard.rationale: The topology scope breadcrumb must expose the current location and preserve keyboard navigation to every broader scope.

topology.overlay.composition.rationale: Canvas overlays must stack in one pointer-safe shared bar, remain keyboard interactive, and remove entrance motion when reduced motion is requested.

design.warning-foreground.token.rationale: Warning text must resolve through one semantic light/dark token and one Tailwind theme alias, not page-local hue classes.

design.warning-foreground.badge.rationale: The shared warning badge must consume semantic foreground, surface, and border tokens so every future feature reuses the same state treatment.

design.sheet.drawer-shadow.boundary.rationale: The four-direction product Sheet owns its tested overlay, focus, motion, and elevation boundary; a one-direction upstream drawer shadow cannot be substituted silently.

design.resource-kind.palette.rationale: The product Badge deliberately exposes typed semantic variants only; resource-kind palette support needs a server-described resource presentation contract before it can be added.

shared-ui.collapse.disclosure.rationale: A controlled disclosure must preserve lazy mounting while keeping retained closed controls out of focus and accessibility traversal, including when reduced motion is requested.

shared-ui.multi-select.controlled.rationale: The reusable picker must filter only its controlled item list, apply bulk changes only to visible values, and leave all displayed strings to the owner-provided labels.

shared-ui.select-menu.dismissal.rationale: The shared select must preserve selection, keyboard Escape, outside-pointer dismissal, focus restoration, and a reduced-motion-safe open indicator.

shared-ui.confirmation-dialog.safety.rationale: The shared confirmation dialog must make owner-provided validation and pending state authoritative before an action can run or a modal can be dismissed.

shared-ui.dialog.nested-escape.rationale: Nested modal Escape handling must close only the topmost dialog and preserve the parent dialog's focus and interaction boundary.

shared-ui.pane-loader.geometry.rationale: A pane-local loading status must keep its decorative spinner centered while owner-provided title and detail occupy a stable bounded label area below it.

helm.release-list.search-shortcut.rationale: The route-owned release-list shortcut must focus the shared typed input without stealing an editable, modal, or already-handled key event.

shared-ui.input.identifier-policy.rationale: The common input must disable browser text mutation for Kubernetes identifiers while retaining an explicit caller override and a typed native ref boundary.

shared-ui.search-pill.input-policy.rationale: Structured search filters must consume the product-owned identifier-safe input primitive instead of restoring a raw browser input.

shared-ui.search-box.lifecycle.rationale: A future collapsible search owner must retain its externally owned focus, duplicate-registration, and blur lifecycle contract.

shared-ui.code-viewer.search.rationale: A future safe code-viewer projection must test find-state, keyboard ownership, and identifier-safe search input against an authorized manifest source.

shared-ui.resource-bar.capacity.rationale: A future utilization bar must test server-observed used, allocatable, marker, and severity data without treating a percentage alone as capacity evidence.

logs.stream.clean-end.adapter.rationale: The authenticated SSE adapter must preserve a typed clean-end reason through the product-owned log stream boundary.

logs.stream.terminal-state.rationale: A clean terminal event must retain discovered workload pods, end the matching tab, and suppress a false retry affordance.

logs.viewer.shared-input.rationale: Log search must consume the reusable accessible input primitive rather than maintaining a second raw input implementation.

logs.viewer.empty-diagnostic.rationale: A future empty-log diagnostic must be a typed, redacted server projection; the tab test will cover its unavailable and rendered states.

logs.workload.empty-diagnostic.rationale: A future workload-empty diagnostic must retain stream identity and be rendered only from an authenticated typed endpoint event.

compare.picker.keyboard.rationale: The compare candidate picker must retain canonical URL replacement, server-authorized candidates, partial inventory evidence, and IME-safe keyboard selection.

resources.physical-topology.stream-lifec.rationale: The typed physical-topology stream must expose connecting before its authenticated browser transport is connected and must keep its bounded delivery policy authoritative.

logs.scheduled-run.target.rationale: A future scheduled-workload log target must prove its server-authorized run identity before it opens the existing bounded log stream.

namespace.scope.rescope.rationale: A future namespace-rescope controller must prove authorized catalog replacement, URL state, and active-session invalidation without browser-derived scope.

issues.severity.server-projection.rationale: The Python queue projection must normalize only the shared typed severity policy and preserve incomplete, informational, and unknown evidence as unavailable.

issues.severity.router-contract.rationale: The additive Issues projection must keep the same authenticated cluster authorization boundary as the legacy RCA timeline while preserving the old strict response route.

issues.severity.frontend-contract.rationale: The additive browser contract must reject contradictory severity availability and leave the legacy timeline schema unchanged for rolling deployment compatibility.

issues.severity.queue-presentation.rationale: The queue must render a badge only for a server-issued tier and must not invent a severity for unavailable source evidence.

issues.severity.queue-order.rationale: The queue must prioritize verified source tiers while preserving server order within equal tiers.

issues.timing.evidence.rationale: A future onset-timing chip requires a typed, event-time Python projection that distinguishes resource creation from a verified healthy regression.

interactions.interaction: an Issues queue receives a server-owned critical or warning presentation tier and renders one semantic badge and rail treatment only when that bounded tier is verified

opsiaPort.rationale: The additive Python projection reuses the typed timeline severity policy: high maps to critical and medium to warning, while low, info, unknown, and incomplete evidence are explicitly unavailable. The old strict timeline endpoint is unchanged; the new UI reads the additive contract and has a bounded one-read rollout fallback only for an absent new route.

interactions.interaction: the issue queue presents verified critical rows before warning rows and retains the server order for equal or unavailable tiers without deriving timestamps or detector state in the browser

opsiaPort.rationale: The product list receives the typed queue tier from the additive authenticated read model, uses shared semantic Badge and StatusMark tokens, and preserves the existing server order within each tier so auto-refresh cannot manufacture an onset time.

interactions.interaction: an issue row can distinguish a failing signal present at resource creation from one that started after a verified healthy interval

opsiaPort.blockedReason: The current immutable RCA timeline has no event-time resource-creation timestamp, verified healthy-window boundary, or detector timing basis. Deriving either from updated_at or current inventory would misstate the incident onset.
opsiaPort.rationale: The timing chip remains unavailable until Python persists a bounded event-time timing projection with explicit evidence completeness; no browser heuristic is added.

interactions.interaction: severity normalization and deterministic queue ordering are verified at the Python contract, browser API, adapter, and presentation boundaries

opsiaPort.rationale: Regression tests prove source-tier normalization, authorization, malformed-response rejection, presentation ordering, and the single 404-only legacy read fallback. Onset timing assertions are intentionally separate and blocked until event-time evidence exists.

interactions.interaction: a side-specific compare picker filters only server-authorized compatible candidates, excludes its source resource, preserves partial-inventory evidence, and maps IME-safe roving keyboard selection to canonical comparison URL state

opsiaPort.rationale: The product candidate endpoint already applies workspace, cluster, and inventory authorization before returning a compatible descriptor set. The route owns canonical URL replacement while the picker reuses the shared identifier-safe input instead of source runtime code.

interactions.interaction: the topology consumer exposes a distinct connecting state until its authenticated realtime browser transport reports connected, and returns to connecting before each new connection attempt

realtime.resume: visibility or sequence-integrity reconnects discard the previous client state and require a fresh server snapshot
realtime.backpressure: the gateway hello policy bounds pending messages and the browser coalesces accepted records at the negotiated maximum frame rate
realtime.merge: only ordered server snapshot and delta records for the active workspace and cluster mutate the overlay; invalid sequence requests a resync

motion.reducedMotion: connecting and connection-state feedback remain semantic while realtime paint coalescing avoids decorative animation dependence.

opsiaPort.rationale: The source delta is limited to connecting lifecycle semantics. Opsia deliberately uses its authenticated typed WebSocket gateway rather than the source EventSource runtime, preserving a stricter negotiated policy, resync, and scope model.

interactions.interaction: scheduled workload kinds route to a retained-run selector before opening the selected run's bounded workload log stream

realtime.resume: a selected immutable run target opens a new authorized stream; a terminal run does not infer a replacement target
realtime.backpressure: the selected stream retains its bounded ordered log buffer and animation-frame batching
realtime.merge: events apply only to the selected immutable run target and its current stream generation

opsiaPort.rationale: The browser now routes a server-issued immutable run UID through the typed scheduled endpoint. Python re-resolves the owner/run UID and exact pod ownership before every persisted stream batch; final page-level picker composition remains in progress.

interactions.interaction: a scheduled workload exposes its retained executions, chooses a valid default run, makes the selected run visible, and forwards only that run to the shared workload log viewer

realtime.resume: a run catalog refresh may replace a missing selection only with a server-authorized default run before the stream opens
realtime.backpressure: run catalog refresh and the selected log stream require independent bounded update policies
realtime.merge: a selected run identity must match the catalog generation and log stream target before its status or lines render

opsiaPort.rationale: The Python catalog now returns retained executions, observed lifecycle counts, a server-selected default run, coverage reasons, and immutable resource references from two bounded queries. The strict browser schema consumes that catalog without deriving Job or pod names; final page-level picker composition remains in progress.

interactions.interaction: a cache-scoped namespace selector exposes only authorized namespaces, applies one replacement scope, communicates the rescope lifecycle, and invalidates incompatible active sessions

opsiaPort.blockedReason: The current Python APIs accept namespace filters but do not project an authorized namespace catalog, cache-scope ownership, rescope lifecycle, or the required invalidation of terminal and port-forward sessions.
opsiaPort.rationale: URL namespace values alone cannot establish whether a namespace is listable, cache-scoped, or safe to switch, so the product retains only its existing normalized filter state until the server contract exists.

interactions.interaction: noninteractive build configuration: shared UI dependency upgrades are represented by the product-owned standalone package baseline

opsiaPort.rationale: The standalone package already pins the updated UI dependency baseline in one product-owned manifest. This is build compatibility evidence only and does not claim that every dependent source surface is ported.

interactions.interaction: noninteractive build configuration: a transitional external TypeScript compiler launcher is exposed for the reusable source package

opsiaPort.blockedReason: The product is one standalone Vite application and pins its supported TypeScript build through `tsc -b`; adding the isolated package's cross-package future-compiler shim would create a second unsupported build authority.
opsiaPort.rationale: The product test records the one supported compiler entrypoint so this source-only transition cannot be mistaken for a completed runtime port.

interactions.interaction: noninteractive warning badge presentation resolves its foreground through a shared semantic token rather than a theme-specific hue class

opsiaPort.rationale: The product-owned Badge now exposes one warning variant that consumes shared status surface, border, and semantic foreground tokens. No feature page owns a copied warning color.

interactions.interaction: noninteractive resource-kind palette extends upstream color choices for workflow and scaled-job resource labels

opsiaPort.blockedReason: The product has no server-described resource presentation palette or typed resource-kind Badge API. Copying upstream kind-to-hue strings into a generic primitive would make browser-owned Kubernetes taxonomy and duplicate feature styling.
opsiaPort.rationale: The shared Badge test keeps the current semantic-only API explicit; workflow and scaled-job colors remain unported until the resource contract owns their presentation metadata.

interactions.interaction: controlled disclosure lazily mounts heavy content, retains it after first open, and removes closed content from keyboard and accessibility traversal while its grid row collapses

motion.reducedMotion: The grid-row disclosure and its rotating caret keep state feedback but suppress transitions when reduced motion is requested.

opsiaPort.rationale: The product-owned primitive uses a controlled state boundary and canonical slots. It retains source lazy-mount behavior while adding `aria-hidden` alongside `inert` so hidden interactive descendants cannot be reached by assistive technology.

interactions.interaction: controlled multi-select verification covers option rows, search threshold, empty states, selected summary, unavailable clear action, and visible-set bulk labels

opsiaPort.rationale: The product test exercises the same reusable picker through actual user interactions instead of source-runtime SSR markup, including owner-controlled selection and completion callbacks.

interactions.interaction: controlled multi-select filters a host-provided item list, toggles checkbox values, applies bulk changes only to visible values, and returns clear and completion events to its owner

opsiaPort.rationale: The product primitive keeps data and all visible copy owner-provided. It does not derive resource kinds, namespaces, authorization, or labels in the browser, so every scoped filter can reuse one behavior safely.

interactions.interaction: single-select menu opens from a named trigger, exposes option selection, dismisses on Escape and outside pointer input without mutation, and indicates open state with a rotating caret

motion.reducedMotion: The open-state caret retains its semantic expanded state while its transform transition is disabled for reduced-motion users.

opsiaPort.rationale: The product-owned Base UI Select supplies the source menu semantics with stronger keyboard and focus handling. Its trigger now owns a shared expanded-state caret motion token rather than feature-local chevrons.

interactions.interaction: confirmation dialog keeps an owner-supplied action unavailable while validation is incomplete, supports custom panel width, and preserves pending dismissal policy

opsiaPort.rationale: The product-owned ConfirmationDialog takes labels, detail, validation, pending state, and custom content from its caller. It centralizes action gating without deriving command data or hardcoding feature copy.

interactions.symbol: DialogPortal Escape dispatch and modal ordering
interactions.interaction: modal portal transfers focus, closes only the topmost dialog on Escape, and keeps nested dialog dismissal from leaking to an outer modal

motion.reducedMotion: Dialog backdrop and panel preserve their open/closed state while animation and duration are disabled for reduced-motion users.

opsiaPort.rationale: The product dialog delegates portal ordering, focus return, and nested dismissal to the shared Base UI primitive. The accessibility test now proves the source topmost-Escape invariant without importing the source runtime.

interactions.symbol: PaneLoader children and bounded label geometry
interactions.interaction: pane-local loading indicator keeps the spinner at the geometric center while an owner-supplied label and optional detail render in a bounded region below it

motion.reducedMotion: The shared spinner keeps status semantics but stops its decorative rotation when reduced motion is requested.

opsiaPort.rationale: The product PaneLoader ports the changed stable-label and optional-detail behavior with the shared accessible Spinner. The unchanged source-specific image asset is intentionally not imported into the product runtime.

interactions.interaction: a reusable text input defaults browser autocorrection and automatic capitalization off for Kubernetes identifiers while allowing an explicit caller override and typed native focus ownership

opsiaPort.rationale: The product-owned Input now exposes a typed forwarded HTMLInputElement ref and applies identifier-safe defaults without taking style, value, validation, or copy ownership away from its caller.

interactions.interaction: a route-owned list shortcut focuses the exact externally owned shared search input instead of a detached local ref

opsiaPort.rationale: The Helm list retains one route-owned shortcut listener and passes its typed ref directly to the shared Input, preventing the prior detached-ref focus failure without DOM queries or selectors.

interactions.interaction: a reusable search wrapper can suppress its own slash registration when a parent already owns the same shortcut

opsiaPort.blockedReason: The product shortcut registry intentionally has no extensible route-scoped single-key registration API or help-overlay descriptor for this generic control. Helm has one route-owned listener, so duplicating the source wrapper registration would create a second shortcut authority.
opsiaPort.rationale: The completed Helm focus path has one owner; reusable registration metadata remains deferred until it can join the product shortcut authority rather than bypass it.

interactions.interaction: a collapsible search owner can react to input blur without forcing the shared input to own expansion state

opsiaPort.blockedReason: The Helm release search is permanently visible and has no typed collapsed/expanded presentation state. Adding a no-op blur callback would not preserve the source lifecycle.
opsiaPort.rationale: This stays explicit until a product route exposes a real owner-controlled collapsible search contract.

interactions.interaction: the editable segment of a structured filter delegates browser text-mutation policy to the one shared typed input primitive

opsiaPort.rationale: The existing structured filter already consumes the shared Input; its regression test now proves the source policy is inherited rather than copied as raw input attributes.

interactions.interaction: the code-viewer find control uses the shared identifier-safe input rather than a raw browser input

opsiaPort.blockedReason: The product has an authorized YAML editor but no server-backed code-viewer/find projection. Adding an isolated client-side find box would not preserve source search, selection, or source-freshness semantics.
opsiaPort.rationale: The shared Input is ready, but no code-viewer surface claims this behavior until its read contract exists.

interactions.interaction: a resource-capacity bar supports a non-alarmist utilization palette, inline label layout, and a separate scheduler-capacity marker

motion.reducedMotion: Any future capacity fill must retain its percentage and threshold meaning while width transitions are disabled for reduced-motion users.

opsiaPort.blockedReason: The current Home projection supplies percentages only; it does not supply typed used, allocatable, request-marker, or scheduling-pressure evidence. Mapping a percentage to the source capacity bar would fabricate a denominator and threshold state in the browser.
opsiaPort.rationale: The existing generic Progress remains correct for determinate operation state. A capacity-specific primitive waits for a server-owned capacity contract.

interactions.interaction: noninteractive Tailwind theme alias exposes the semantic warning foreground to shared component utilities

opsiaPort.rationale: The product @theme alias maps `text-warning-foreground` to one shared CSS variable, keeping the upstream warning-text behavior available without feature-local aliases.

interactions.interaction: noninteractive warning text foreground supplies distinct accessible light and dark values

opsiaPort.rationale: The product token layer owns the exact upstream light `#92400E` and dark `#FBBF24` foreground values, exposed only through the reusable warning-foreground semantic name.

interactions.interaction: noninteractive dark drawer elevation retunes a one-direction horizontal shadow and adds a light outline

opsiaPort.blockedReason: The product Sheet is a tested four-direction overlay primitive, while this upstream token defines only one horizontal drawer shadow. Applying that left-facing shadow to top, bottom, and opposite-side panels would create a directionally incorrect elevation treatment.
opsiaPort.rationale: The product keeps its canonical Sheet elevation, focus, overlay, and reduced-motion boundary visible in the primitive test. A directional shadow port is deferred until a side-aware token contract covers all four product panel directions.

interactions.interaction: noninteractive asset: Argo CD provider mark is preserved byte-for-byte behind the shared GitOps provider identity registry

opsiaPort.rationale: The canonical shared registry now owns the exact product asset and its provenance test. No GitOps, application, or topology product surface consumes this mark yet, so this evidence records only the completed static-asset boundary and does not claim UI parity.

interactions.interaction: noninteractive asset: Flux provider mark is preserved byte-for-byte behind the shared GitOps provider identity registry

opsiaPort.rationale: The canonical shared registry now owns the exact product asset and its provenance test. No GitOps, application, or topology product surface consumes this mark yet, so this evidence records only the completed static-asset boundary and does not claim UI parity.

interactions.interaction: noninteractive document configuration: a reusable host stylesheet isolates its mount selector from the host application root

opsiaPort.blockedReason: The product is a standalone web and desktop application, not an embeddable host stylesheet. Its single `#root` mount is intentional and the source mount identifier is a prohibited legacy product term.
opsiaPort.rationale: The document test proves that the product has exactly one explicit root and local bootstrap script without copying the isolated host-library mount convention.

interactions.interaction: noninteractive build configuration: web dependency and lint upgrades are represented by the current standalone product manifest

opsiaPort.rationale: The product manifest already pins the matching browser dependency and lint/test baseline under its own package boundary. This proves only build compatibility, not a claim that source library consumers are supported.

interactions.symbol: package.json main, types, exports, files, and sideEffects
interactions.interaction: noninteractive build configuration: the source app publishes a reusable browser library with host-facing entrypoints

opsiaPort.blockedReason: The product ships one authenticated web application and a Tauri shell, not a reusable browser library; publishing source entrypoints would expose the isolated runtime and violate the product boundary.
opsiaPort.rationale: The product manifest test proves that no library main or export surface is silently introduced.

interactions.interaction: noninteractive build configuration: source library scripts delegate to a transitional compiler launcher and package-local test command

opsiaPort.blockedReason: The product owns one TypeScript project-reference build and whole-console test command. The source transitional compiler launcher and source-local test scope cannot be adopted without adding a parallel package build contract.
opsiaPort.rationale: The product test keeps the supported build and test commands explicit while preserving the source delta as blocked rather than ported.

interactions.interaction: public timeline primitives compose through one product-owned route surface

opsiaPort.rationale: The product route already owns the shell and contract boundary; the upstream barrel is reference-only.

interactions.interaction: range, lens, and zoom-rung calculations keep a positive bounded selection

opsiaPort.blockedReason: TimelineCapabilityDescriptor does not yet describe lens minimums or server-approved zoom rungs.
opsiaPort.rationale: The browser must not invent range limits or a day-based zoom ladder.

interactions.interaction: pointer and keyboard lens changes clamp within the selected query range

motion.reducedMotion: range changes expose their final value without animated movement

opsiaPort.blockedReason: Server capability data for minimum lens window, keyboard step, and zoom rungs is absent.
opsiaPort.rationale: The retained strip must use descriptor values rather than hardcoded range arithmetic.

interactions.interaction: timeline marker and severity presentation remains semantically stable

opsiaPort.rationale: Current event cards already consume typed activity, event type, and severity values.

interactions.interaction: semantic event identity drives consistent list and lane markers

opsiaPort.rationale: Typed event labels and views are product-owned and do not import upstream renderers.

interactions.interaction: activity, kinds, deletion, search, and selected-event filters round-trip through URL state

opsiaPort.blockedReason: The server has no facet response to drive filter availability and independent counts.
opsiaPort.rationale: URL parsing exists, but dynamic toolbar choices must come from an authorized aggregation.

interactions.interaction: filter predicates use canonical activity and kind selections without client fixture data

opsiaPort.blockedReason: Facet aggregation and the server control catalog are not yet defined.
opsiaPort.rationale: Existing predicates accept filters, but the UI cannot safely infer selectable values or counts.

interactions.interaction: importance, recency, and name lane ordering is deterministic for one authorized projection

opsiaPort.blockedReason: The snapshot has events but no server lane aggregation or sort projection for large timelines.
opsiaPort.rationale: Client-only grouping would duplicate data logic and exceed smooth-update limits.

interactions.interaction: lane order follows a server-defined grouping and sort projection

opsiaPort.blockedReason: Grouping and sort enum values exist, but the backend does not emit a bounded lane projection.
opsiaPort.rationale: The product must not hardcode upstream lane ordering heuristics.

interactions.interaction: live and frozen range state preserves its cursor and reports unseen events

realtime.resume: opaque cursor resume
realtime.backpressure: server negotiated frame-rate coalescing
